signature.name: Keyboard path home
signature.description: Can a keyboard or screen-reader visitor reach and activate Home in three Tabs or fewer, with a strong visible focus indicator and link names that make sense out of context?

group-a.signature_why: Home is the first link (1 Tab) with a 3px outline plus offset, but the 4-loaf-4 heading is announced as 'No. 4, 0, a loaf with a bite out, 4' and the 375px layout sits off-centre.
group-a.loved: Home is first in a labelled nav, 48px targets, bold hours before decoration, reduced motion gated correctly.
group-a.docked: The loaf-as-zero image has an awkward spoken label, and the self-confessed unresolved off-centre 375px capture.

group-b.signature_why: Home is the first link (1 Tab), 56px targets, 3px rust outline, art is aria-hidden so screen readers get a clean headline; the nav has no label and Hours is a bare name.
group-b.loved: Large 56px links come before the art, the decorative loaf is hidden from assistive tech, and the path is shown as plain text as well.
group-b.docked: The oversized loaf graphic carries the URL as unreadable-for-AT art, and the unlabelled nav is a missed landmark name.

group-c.signature_why: Home is the first link (1 Tab), full-width 48px rows with descriptive hints, an inverted-fill focus state with the default outline kept, and the hours table is real semantic content with today marked in text, not colour alone.
group-c.loved: The week table states 'today' and 'no bake' in words, not colour only, so it is just as charming for everyone; the link names have helpful context.
group-c.docked: Focus relies on a fill inversion rather than a custom ring, and the struck-through path text is hard to read, so the Full week link name is vague.
